sylvia: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on TP + fused-attn path after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak. p50 token latency up ~80% on our 8xA100 perf job :eyes:

sylvia: Summary: before=52ms, after=92ms (same model/checkpoint). Throughput also drops ~30%.

sylvia: Repro command I used: `./bench/run_perf.py --model gpt-10b --tp 2 --pp 1 --bs 8 --seq 2048 --kernel-policy=auto`

sylvia: Quick nvprof snapshot (cropped):
```
NCCL AllReduce  38%
FlashAttn kernel  22%
CUDA memcpy      10%
Other kernels     30%
```

matt: ack. did this coincide with the change that prefers flash_attn_v2 for short-seq shapes?

sylvia: yes. kernel-picker now prefers flash_attn_v2 when seq <= 512 and head_dim % 64 == 0. regression shows up even for seq 256 shards because TP all-gather patterns make the effective per-gpu seq shape different.

rao: interesting — could be comm/compute overlap getting worse because of KV prefetch ordering. we added async prefetch to start KV fetch earlier but it may serialize with the TP allgather handshake.

jess: any flamegraphs or timelines? even a short perf report helps.

sylvia: pasted a timeline snippet below — note the large NCCL stall after QKV all-gather and before flash kernel launches:
```
[0.0s] QKV all-gather start
[0.045s] QKV all-gather end -> NCCL allreduce (blocking)
[0.110s] flash_attn kernel queued (waits for comm)
[0.190s] kernel runs
```

ankit: that blocking NCCL window is the issue. with TP shards, the all-gather size increased due to our padding change in the batching heuristic. we're creating more uneven shards so more frequent smaller allreduces instead of fewer large ones.

matt: can you share the batching config? maybe dynamic batching pushed more partially-filled microbatches.

sylvia: current batching config (from the perf job):
```
batching.max_batch_tokens = 65536
batching.max_latency_ms = 12
batching.prefer_full_batches = true
kv.prefetch_enabled = true
kv.prefetch_stride = 128
kernel_policy = auto
```

rao: prefer_full_batches + prefetch_stride 128 = suspicious. For TP the stride affects how KV shards align; misaligned strides cause extra cross-GPU traffic. Suggest prefetch_stride=64 for TP profiles.

jess: also try forcing kernel_policy=legacy for the run to see if kernel-picker is the main culprit (flash_v2 may not handle the post-allgather alignment well).

ci-bench-bot: perf-run 1935012345-sub1 completed. Results attached: p50=91.8ms, p95=210ms, allreduce_time_avg=42.1ms.

matt: thanks. can you snapshot nccl tests? run the microbench: `./tools/nccl_probe --gpus 8 --size 4MB --iters 500` and paste numbers.

sylvia: ran it — bandwidth ok but latency higher than baseline: latency ~1.6ms -> 2.9ms for small messages. suspect small allreduce count increased.

ankit: mitigation plan: 1) revert kernel-picker change for TP experiments, 2) lower prefetch_stride to 64, 3) tune batching.max_batch_tokens to 256k for perf tests to coalesce more tokens into fewer allgathers. If that helps, we can make a smarter shard-aware kernel-selection: use post-shard effective shape not pre-shard local shape.

jess: +1 on shard-aware selection. also add an instrumentation point: count allgather ops per request and report percentile. want to know if requests generating >3 allgathers cause the tail.

matt: willing to own the temporary revert. sylvia can you run the three variants and paste the mini report?

sylvia: will run now, posting short summary in ~15m.

sylvia (15m later): quick results: baseline (revert kernel-picker, prefetch_stride=128, max_batch_tokens=65k): p50=54ms.
variant A (keep picker, prefetch_stride=64): p50=60ms.
variant B (picker reverted, prefetch_stride=64, max_batch_tokens=256k): p50=49ms, throughput +28%.

matt: that's pretty clear. variant B looks best. I'll open a PR to revert the picker change and we'll follow up with a kernel-picker PR that queries TP-shard effective shape.

rao: also add a regression test in perf harness: run a TP fused-attn profile with varying strides and assert allreduce_count doesn't exceed threshold for given seq len.

jess: nice detective work. please add the nvprof traces to the perf job artifact bucket and tag them. i'll create the follow-up issue for kernel-picker heuristics. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sylvia: uploaded traces to s3://perf-artifacts/1935012345/. PR and issue links coming.
